summary: Keep each GitHub observer's poll cursor in the polling member's plugin database, <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3, instead of in observer.observed claims that replicate to every member.

replay.detail: No claim is rewritten or replayed. Claims older builds wrote keep their cursor field and stay valid.

schema.detail: The claims database schema and its version are unchanged. New local file <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3 (PRAGMA user_version 1, one table observer_cursors keyed by observer subject), created on first start. It never syncs and is not in a backup; deleting it costs each observer one baseline poll. A build that finds a newer version refuses the file and keeps cursors in memory until restart.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes. No fleet barrier or coordinated upgrade: each member changes only its own writes.

compatibility.detail: Claim vocabulary (contract change C1): observer.observed for observer/github/* no longer carries cursor; it keeps status, revision, changed and attempt. The field stays in the claim registry (/v1/schema, st schema claims) as optional, because older members still write it. No client-v0 change. Mixed versions: an older poller keeps writing cursors until it upgrades; on upgrade a member adopts the cursor in its newest observer.observed claim once, then reads its plugin database. A member that takes over polling without a cursor (any build) reads every open item once, as a first poll; items it already recorded compare equal to their recorded facts, so nothing is delivered twice. An older member reads the newest cursor an older build wrote, if any, which is an earlier point than the new poller's; it re-reads from there and likewise delivers nothing twice.

downtime.detail: No startup migration. The first poll after upgrade continues from the claim's cursor; it is not a baseline.

manual.detail: No operator action. The plugin directory is created beneath the state directory.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to an older build is supported: it finds no cursor in this build's claims (or an older one) and baselines each repository once, within the github-admission hourly budget, delivering nothing twice. The plugin database is ignored by older builds and may be deleted.
